title: Synapse-count weights gave no clear reduction in repeated coherence change in 35 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested whether synapse-count weights reduced changes in a combined complex coherence summary in one leech circuit. Anatomy and activity came from the same ganglion. The primary sample had 35 inputs to motor neuron DE-3R and 271 contacts. Mean squared readout change was 0.02256 across two swim trials and 0.07515 across three left-bend trials. These scores were 1.37 and 1.27 times the exact means for shuffled count assignments. Lower-tail label probabilities were 0.76795 and 0.73520; both Holm values were 1.00. Changes showed net reinforcement across inputs rather than net cancellation in all three selected cohorts. An exact shuffle formula separates the expected effect of unequal weights from input assignment. This is a null result for a summary-based model. One animal, few trials, shared reference signals, uncertain input matches, and missing signs and spectral errors limit the result. The weighted sum is not a measured synaptic current or a test of behavior reliability. Original code, aggregate draws, a figure, source hashes, and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External raw records and record-level tables are not bundled.

display.caption: Observed count weights did not reduce repeated coherence change relative to shuffled count assignments in one leech input circuit. Lower values indicate less absolute change. Label draws are not animals.

citations.reason: Prior count association with individual repeated coherence. We test a combined count-weighted summary and cross-input changes.
Prior shared population calibration. We test anatomical weights without a fitted calibration map.
